title: API lemma expressing s(N) as N/d₁ + N/d₂ + N/d₃ (IMO 2025 P4)
intent: Establish an interface for s N (the sum of the three largest proper divisors, defined by indexing into the descending sort of N.properDivisors): the lemma rewrites it as N / d₁ + N / d₂ + N / d₃ where d₁ < d₂ < d₃ are the three smallest divisors of N greater than 1, so later lemmas reason about s through this arithmetic form instead of unfolding the sort.

parent.name: lem_s_N_smallest_divisors
parent.statement: lemma lem_s_N_smallest_divisors (N : ℕ) (h_card : 3 ≤ N.properDivisors.card) : let d₁ := ((N.divisors.erase 1).sort (· ≤ ·))[0]!; let d₂ := ((N.divisors.erase 1).sort (· ≤ ·))[1]!; let d₃ := ((N.divisors.erase 1).sort (· ≤ ·))[2]!; s N = N / d₁ + N / d₂ + N / d₃

children.name: h_largest
children.closed_by: list equality (N.properDivisors.sort (· ≥ ·)) = List.map (fun d => N / d) ((N.divisors.erase 1).sort (· ≤ ·)) by List.eq_of_perm_of_sorted (Sorted+Nodup via induction, Perm via toFinset, lines 84-108), then rcases n : Finset.sort … <;> aesop (line 109)

children.name: main goal
children.statement: s N = N / d₁ + N / d₂ + N / d₃

applicability.goal_shape: A goal mentioning s N where s is defined by an if-guarded sum over the descending sort of N.properDivisors; the interface lemma rewrites s N into N / d₁ + N / d₂ + N / d₃ over the ascending sorted list N.divisors.erase 1.
applicability.use_when: many client lemmas need s N in an arithmetic form and would otherwise each unfold the sort; the companion list (ascending divisors greater than 1) is the natural indexing for the argument.
applicability.avoid_when: the sort-based form itself is what the proof needs (e.g. comparing the three largest proper divisors directly), or the side condition 3 ≤ N.properDivisors.card is hard for clients to discharge.

claims.claim: The parent lem_s_N_smallest_divisors closes from two children: the key invariant h_largest (lines 80-109) establishes that the three largest proper divisors equal N/d₁, N/d₂, N/d₃, and then unfold s; aesop (line 110) discharges the goal s N = N/d₁ + N/d₂ + N/d₃.

The interface lemma is reused at seven sites without re-unfolding the sort: directly at lines 171 (apply lem_s_N_smallest_divisors) and 590 (convert lem_s_N_smallest_divisors N h_card using 1), and via lem_s_N_formula at lines 300, 331, 368, 551, 627.
claims.evidence: grep of the copied file code/HarmonicLean/IMO2025P4_solve2.lean for 'lem_s_N_smallest_divisors' (hits: 74, 171, 590) and 'lem_s_N_formula' (hits: 163, 300, 331, 368, 551, 627)

claims.claim: The authors state the lemma's purpose in the doc comment above it: "If 1 < d₁ < d₂ < d₃ < … are the positive divisors of N greater than 1 in increasing order, then the three largest proper divisors of N are N/d₁, N/d₂, and N/d₃."

The same interface pattern recurs one level up: lem_s_N_formula (lines 163-193) is a second API lemma that rewrites s N as the rational reciprocal formula (N : ℚ) * (1/d₁ + 1/d₂ + 1/d₃), and it consumes lem_s_N_smallest_divisors at line 171 rather than unfolding s.

metrics.how_counted: parent_proof_lines = lines 74-110 of the copied file; children = the h_largest key invariant (lines 80-109) and the final unfold (line 110); reuses counted by grep of the copied file for 'lem_s_N_smallest_divisors' (direct: 171, 590) and 'lem_s_N_formula' (300, 331, 368, 551, 627)

consequences: The interface lemma carries the definition's side condition 3 ≤ N.properDivisors.card as an explicit hypothesis h_card, so every client must discharge it (cheap here, since all clients already assume h_card). It changes the representation of s N from a sort-based term to an arithmetic sum: a client that needs the descending-sort form itself must unfold s or use a different lemma. It also adds a dependency on the companion list N.divisors.erase 1 sorted ascending. The proof of the interface itself is the bulk of the work (the h_largest sub-argument, lines 80-109), so the move pays off only when the interface is reused.
